E1.evidence: Issue gives the scenario (rqt_controller_manager open, controller manager stopped, e.g. simulation restarted) and the traceback ending in "RuntimeError: Could not contact service /controller_manager/list_controllers"; the maintainer-authored PR #1273 (merged 2024-01-08, merge commit 2d82de84ba0ce746ecc6d3db58b0e12b2533bd2c) confirms and fixes it. -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1223

E2.evidence: The failure is an unhandled exception in rqt_controller_manager's own polling logic: when any controller manager (a correct one, legitimately stopped for a simulation restart) is unreachable, controller_manager_services.service_caller raises "RuntimeError(f'Could not contact service {service_name}')" and _list_controllers does not catch it, which "raises an error and kills the window" (issue). No wrong value, frame, unit, name, type or timing crosses the boundary; the provider is simply absent and the consumer crashes, which would happen with any correct peer that is stopped. The fix wraps the call in "try: ... except RuntimeError as e: print(e); return []" in rqt_controller_manager/controller_manager.py and adds an optional service_timeout argument (default 10.0) to the controller_manager_services helpers so the GUI polls with 2.0/self._cm_update_freq; the existing interface is unchanged. -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/pull/1273. Borderline: the scenario is a provider stop/restart while the consumer keeps polling (a SWITCH-like lifecycle), but the tree's step-2 example (a crash in one unit's own logic) fits better than any interface class.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated past E2 (candidate operation would be SWITCH: the controller manager stopped/restarted while the rqt plugin keeps polling service /controller_manager/list_controllers).

E4.evidence: Traceback and window crash documented in the issue and PR #1273 'Before' section.
